answer: Slash-forfeiting locked bond resists sybils: each identity locks collateral that unlocks only after a long maturation, and any identity caught misbehaving forfeits its entire locked bond to an honest pool. A river of fakes must each lock a full bond for the whole window, so capital-at-risk grows linearly with head count, and a single falcon-eyed detection burns that head's whole pearl of stake. An honest agent locks once and recovers it at maturity. Precondition: detection probability times bond exceeds per-head expected gain, so a farm's expected forfeiture outruns its profit.
